Every conversation follows a predictable sequence of events. You only need to write @aiui.reply to start; add the other decorators whenever you want custom greetings, per-chat setup, or clean-up.

Every decorator works with both async def and plain def. Decorator Alias When it runs Typical use @aiui.welcome — Once when an empty chat loads Show a friendly greeting above starter cards @aiui.on_chat_start — Once per chat, right before its first reply Initialize per-chat memory, DB client, or agent @aiui.reply @aiui.on_message Every time the user sends a message Call your model, stream tokens, run tools @aiui.cancel @aiui.on_stop When the user clicks Stop mid-reply Log cancellation or clean up an external job @aiui.goodbye @aiui.on_chat_end When the chat's last browser tab closes Close database connections or temporary files Annotate your @aiui.reply parameter as str (async def on_message(text: str)) to receive plain text. Omit the annotation (or type it as MessageContext) when you also need message.session_id, message.agent_name, or message.attachments.
Save this as app.py and run aiui run app.py:

Stopping a reply: Pressing Stop cancels the running @aiui.reply task (asyncio.CancelledError at the next await), immediately halting slow model calls or tool loops. Exceptions: If @aiui.reply raises an error, the UI displays the error cleanly beneath anything already streamed and preserves it on reload. Per-chat isolation: aiui.user_session is scoped to the current chat session, so two users talking at the same time never overwrite each other's state. See Handler context.
Stream tokens, ask interactive follow-up questions and add clickable buttons. Save conversations to disk or SQL so users can resume later.
